_limits: THE MANIFEST MAKES RECORDS DURABLE, NOT TRUE. A quote entered wrongly at creation time is preserved faithfully, hashed, and dated forever — initial verification is the single point of failure, and it has demonstrably failed once (col-prostate: a quote recorded as 'confirmed directly' that was never at the named source, evidenced by a Wayback snapshot predating the verification). The structural checks cannot reach that class; nothing can, except care at entry.
_ruling_statistics: Downgrade-to-illustrative works only for values with an honest illustrative home (colour). It does NOT work for statistics: a user reads '~92%' as fact regardless of labelling. For statistical claims the options are RE-SOURCE (durably-addressed) or REMOVE from the screen — no middle.
_backfill_method: Identifier backfill (2026-09-04): PubMed eutils esearch/esummary with a MULTI-FIELD AGREEMENT GATE — first-author surname + publication year + (journal when recorded) + topic-consistency, and EXACTLY ONE candidate may pass; ambiguous or partial matches are refused, never guessed. Backfilled identifiers carry method+date and DO NOT have the evidentiary weight of identifiers recorded at entry time: they assert 'this recorded metadata resolves uniquely to this paper', not 'this paper was verified to support the claim'. Triage semantics: status=no-match (author+year yields zero PubMed hits) is the strong entry-time-error signature (the Wang/Park case); status=no-field-match is NOT a defect list — it mixes common-surname retrieval misses, retmax truncation, and title-topic gate strictness, and means 'not auto-resolvable', nothing more.
